text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer. The first step is identifying the bug, which means figuring out why your code isn't doing what you expect. A systematic approach helps here: instead of guessing, you isolate the problem by testing small parts of your code one by one. Debugging tools, such as breakpoints in an IDE, allow you to pause the program and inspect variable values at specific moments. Logging is another powerful technique—it involves printing messages to a console to track the flow of execution. By combining these methods, you can find and fix errors efficiently without wasting hours on random changes.
